review.assessment: The draft introduces a new solution.sh that attempts word-frequency counting by translating spaces to newlines, sorting alphabetically, and using uniq -c. It fails to meet requirements for case-insensitivity, comprehensive whitespace splitting, sort ordering, and output formatting.

findings.actual: treats uppercase/lowercase variants as distinct words and sorts by ASCII codepoint order first
findings.call: echo "the cat the DOG" | bash solution.sh
findings.defect: Case sensitivity not handled / casing wrong

findings.actual: fails to split on \t, grouping "a\tb" into a single malformed token instead of separate words
findings.defect: Ignores tabs and newlines as word separators

findings.actual: sorts all lines alphabetically first, then counts runs of identical lines, ignoring the required numerical sort
findings.call: echo "z z y y x" | bash solution.sh
findings.defect: Sort order is alphabetical before counting, not count-descending with alphabetical tie-breaks

findings.actual: outputs with system-dependent space/tab prefixes (e.g., "      2 a") instead of the requested COUNT WORD format
findings.defect: Output format includes leading whitespace padding from uniq -c
